subject.title: fix(doctor): warn when HTTP(S)_PROXY is set without tools.web.fetch.useTrustedEnvProxy

question: After the `NO_PROXY=*` false-positive is fixed, should OpenClaw warn in doctor, status, and deep security audit whenever HTTP(S) proxy variables exist but trusted proxy routing is not enabled, including explicit `false`?
rationale: The implementation adds a new cross-command diagnostic and deliberately warns operators who may have explicitly rejected the weaker DNS-pinning boundary; source correctness cannot decide the desired warning scope or noise policy.

options.title: Keep all three warnings
options.body: Land the diagnostic in doctor, status, and deep security audit after correcting the current-main NO_PROXY behavior and refreshing proof.

options.title: Narrow to doctor
options.body: Expose the guidance only in doctor to reduce recurring status and security-audit noise for explicit opt-outs.

options.title: Keep documentation only
options.body: Close the PR and rely on the existing web-fetch documentation without adding command diagnostics.

recommendation.title: Keep all three warnings
recommendation.body: Land the diagnostic in doctor, status, and deep security audit after correcting the current-main NO_PROXY behavior and refreshing proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The trusted proxy opt-in and most of the proxy environment contract originate from this owner’s current-main history.
